name: Candidates in the order the stated rules give
purpose: The work that competes for attention comes back in the order the rules a person states or the data carries give for it.
record: Invented, neutral cases that each exercise one generic rule (the person's own rank, nearest deadline, oldest ask, people waiting, time since a nudge, blocked items, and what the person stated: kind order, explicit order, deferral, feedback, not-before, only some kinds); a consumer's own ordering rules are scored by the consumer's own arm over cases built on this metric; one number: the share of cases whose whole order equals the reviewed order, balanced with cost and time by [balance.prioritization], weights and budgets fixed before any arm was scored. Mean pairwise agreement is in the details.
disadvantages: Few cases, all invented to exercise one rule each, so a rule that only a real system's data shows is not measured here; weights derived from implied priorities are not yet compared with what a person confirms.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the arm and its rivals were recorded on the same cases]
command: esoi run prioritization --impl stated_fields; esoi run prioritization --impl as_given
